newsitem.title: USA: U.S. layoffs down 51 pct Aug vs July - Challenger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. layoffs down 51 pct Aug vs July - Challenger.

text.p: Announced U.S. job cuts declined 51 percent in August from July, according to a monthly employment report by Challenger, Gray and Christmas Inc.

The August layoffs total was 20,309, the lowest level in 16 months and a 51 percent decline from July's 41,843, the report said. Last month's total was 39 percent lower than the number of layoffs in August 1995, it said.

"One month does not make a trend," John Challenger, executive vice president of Challenger, Gray and Christmas, said in a statement. "We cannot predict that job cuts will remain at the August low level."
U.S. employers announced 332,665 layoffs in the first eight months of 1996, up 24 percent from last year's total for the same period, the report said.
On average 41,583 jobs were cut each from January through August, compared with 33,605 for the same period last year, it said.

"In the previous months of this year we saw significant downsizing, while at the same time some key industries experienced severe spot labor shortages," John Challenger said. "Under these conditions the paradox of deep downsizing and labor shortages cannot be sustained."

Mass job cuts in the semiconductor and integrated-circuit industry added to the August layoff total, the report said. Nine major manufacturers in that sector announced downsizings last month, it said.
